synthesis.trait: Greets John with warmth and a forgiving smile, reflecting an easy familiarity/history between them
Presents as an apologetic, hospitable host trying to maintain normal domestic routine (coffee, a decorated home, a birthday cake) despite being a struggling single mother
Shows visible signs of strain and substance use beneath a functioning exterior (strung out, smoking, working a service job)
When cornered or physically restrained, resorts to manipulation, false threats, or denial to escape confrontation

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Shows visible signs of strain and substance use beneath a functioning exterior
turning_points.what_changes: From merely appearing 'strung out' while working, she now explicitly and deliberately takes an ecstasy pill in a bar bathroom -- an overt act of drug use rather than an implied condition.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Shows visible signs of strain and substance use beneath a functioning exterior
turning_points.what_changes: Direct continuation of the pill she just swallowed -- she is now visibly rolling on molly on the dance floor, the same intoxication event playing out.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Shows visible signs of strain and substance use beneath a functioning exterior
turning_points.what_changes: Still high from the same night's molly, she carries that intoxication directly into an interaction with John, mocking his concern about her missing daughter's case rather than engaging with it.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Shows visible signs of strain and substance use beneath a functioning exterior
turning_points.what_changes: Immediately after being dragged outside by John, she reacts with hostile anger -- the same confrontation continuing without a break in time or location.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Shows visible signs of strain and substance use beneath a functioning exterior
turning_points.what_changes: Her reaction escalates past simple anger into a calculated manipulative threat (falsely claiming she'll scream rape) to escape John's grip -- a qualitatively more serious, weaponized act of self-preservation than any anger shown before.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: When cornered or physically restrained, resorts to manipulation, false threats, or denial to escape confrontation
turning_points.what_changes: Immediately after the threat and being pulled back, she voices flat denial ('She's not gone... everything will be fine') -- the same escape attempt continuing but now revealing genuine delusion rather than mere tactic.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: When cornered or physically restrained, resorts to manipulation, false threats, or denial to escape confrontation
turning_points.what_changes: The same confrontation carries into the parking lot: she again denies anything is wrong ('Nothing is going on'), then her shielding of both O'Shea and John at gunpoint exposes her entanglement in the drug dealing tied to Mackie's death.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Presents as an apologetic, hospitable host trying to maintain normal domestic routine despite being a struggling single mother
turning_points.what_changes: She again pushes someone -- now O'Shea instead of John -- to keep working Holly's case, directly echoing her earlier plea to John for help.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Presents as an apologetic, hospitable host trying to maintain normal domestic routine despite being a struggling single mother
turning_points.what_changes: Beyond simply asking, she now offers to pay John herself and directs O'Shea to give him money -- an active financial commitment and recruitment effort exceeding her earlier verbal request for help.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Presents as an apologetic, hospitable host trying to maintain normal domestic routine despite being a struggling single mother
turning_points.what_changes: In the same conversation, she goes further and names Reggie directly as a suspect, actively supplying dangerous information to help solve the case.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: When cornered or physically restrained, resorts to manipulation, false threats, or denial to escape confrontation
turning_points.what_changes: Where she once flatly denied reality and demanded to be left alone, she now breaks down, admits fault ('I know I could've been a better mom'), and vows to get clean -- a direct reversal of her earlier denial into raw acceptance and resolve.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Presents as an apologetic, hospitable host trying to maintain normal domestic routine despite being a struggling single mother
turning_points.what_changes: Her earlier plea 'you gotta find her... please' is answered here: she instantly knows Holly is dead the moment she sees John, collapsing into hysterics -- the hope she fought to sustain is now conclusively extinguished.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Presents as an apologetic, hospitable host trying to maintain normal domestic routine despite being a struggling single mother
turning_points.what_changes: Directly following the collapse, at the wake she remains in the same hollowed grief -- 'part of her has died, and without any more tears to shed for it' -- the same loss continuing into its aftermath.
